messages:
sam-support: Hey @tina-netops - customer AcmeCorp (private VPC) reporting failures during model load + telemetry sending after pulling a new model. They see TLS errors and occasional 504s from our fetches. Can you advise allowlist?

sam-support: Quick context: deployed Redwood Private in their AWS account, NAT+FW rules are locked down. They say package installs (pip/npm) also fail during deploy.

sam-support: Error snippets from their agent: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z ERROR fetch_manifest: GET https://models.redwood-inference.com/v1/models/acme/manifest -> error: tls: handshake timeout
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z WARN runtime: failed to download artifact: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
curl: (7) Failed to connect to telemetry.redwood-inference.com port 443: Connection timed out
```

sam-support: Repro steps they ran: pip install -r requirements.txt inside deployment job -> fails resolving files.pythonhosted.org; model pull fails at runtime. They attached tcpdump and say DNS resolves to internal proxy.

tina-netops: Thanks, Sam. Can you paste the minimal list of FQDNs they need to allow? Also confirm whether they NAT egress to a fixed IP range (we may need to provide IPs).

sam-support: Pasting what eng gave earlier (please verify):
- auth.redwood-inference.com (443) - OAuth/token + auth checks
- api.redwood-inference.com (443) - control plane API
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com (443) - telemetry ingestion (POST /v1/ingest)
- models.redwood-inference.com (443) - model manifests + variant metadata
- registry.redwood-inference.com (443) - model artifact registry (may redirect to cloud storage)
- packages: pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, github.com (releases)
- cloud storage: storage.googleapis.com, *.s3.amazonaws.com (for model artifact downloads)
- model signing/keys: keys.redwood-inference.com (443)

alex-eng: That's mostly correct. Additional notes:
- We rely on TLS SNI, so firewalls/proxies must allow TLS SNI (or not terminate TLS) to avoid x509 issues. If they perform TLS interception, the cert errors are expected.
- For registry/model artifacts we sometimes redirect to signed URLs on storage.googleapis.com or on s3. That means allowlist both the registry domain and the cloud storage domains.
- Telemetry endpoint: telemetry.redwood-inference.com:443, method=POST, JSON, content-type application/json. Please allow outbound TCP 443 and not block large POST bodies.

alex-eng: Suggested quick checks they can run (paste into their bastion):
```
# DNS
dig +short models.redwood-inference.com
# TLS handshake
openssl s_client -connect models.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername models.redwood-inference.com -brief
# simple curl against telemetry
curl -v https://telemetry.redwood-inference.com/v1/ingest -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"test":1}' || true
```

maria-sre: If they need IPs for firewall rules, advise them that our outbound IPs for hosted infra change (we can provide a current CIDR list on request). Recommended policy: allow by FQDN + port where possible. If they require static IPs, we'll open a ticket to publish current ranges and a webhook for updates.

maria-sre: Also check their egress proxy configuration: if they use an HTTPS proxy, ensure it allows CONNECT to port 443 to those FQDNs and does not MITM TLS (or if it does, the CA cert must be trusted on the host JVM/container). The x509 errors point to TLS interception.

robin-cs: Customer says their infra team is nervous about broad allowlists. They asked for a minimal set for a "model-only" runtime (no package installs). Recommendation: allowlist only: models.redwood-inference.com, registry.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.redwood-inference.com, auth.redwood-inference.com, and cloud storage domains. For package installs, also allow pypi domains / npm.

robin-cs: They also asked whether telemetry can be turned off temporarily to confirm model pull is the blocker. Short answer: yes, they can disable telemetry in Private config (set telemetry.enabled=false) to isolate. But model registry downloads will still be required.

sam-support: I ran the openssl test for them; output shows a TLS cert with CN=redwood-inference.com but chain has proxy CA. So likely MITM. They can push CA to system trust store.

tina-netops: Action items for the customer (to share back):
1) Allow outbound TCP 443 to the FQDN list (above). If possible, allow by domain rather than IPs.
2) Allow traffic to storage.googleapis.com and *.s3.amazonaws.com for artifact downloads.
3) If they terminate TLS/intercept, install their proxy CA in container host JVM and system trust stores.
4) If they require IPs, ask them to provide NAT IPs; we will respond with current CIDR ranges and add to ticket for updates.
5) Run diagnostics and paste dig / openssl / curl outputs.

sam-support: I'll send them a checklist and request the dig/openssl outputs + whether they use an egress proxy.

infra-bot: NOTE: If customer needs pinned IPs, open PR #4622 to publish current egress ranges to the docs and set a reminder to update when ranges change.

maria-sre: Also mention ephemeral signed URLs: model artifact downloads may be short-lived URLs; blocking redirects or HEAD/GET to storage endpoints can cause 403 if not allowed.

tina-netops: Thanks everyone. Sam, please paste the customer's replies once they run the checks and we'll follow up with an IP list if needed. :thumbsup:
